title: Demultiplex background worker pipeline and simplify cache operation path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: The monolithic background worker pipeline that handles async flushes, post-batch bookkeeping, and KV cache maintenance has accrued a lot of implicit state and edge-case handling. This ticket splits the pipeline into explicit micro-steps, introduces a single clear contract for cache read/write operations, and removes duplicated scheduling logic. Goals: reduce tail latency variance, simplify reasoning for future GC/freeze changes, and make the scheduler path auditable and testable.
rationale: Over the past year we've patched the background runner to handle more responsibilities (metrics aggregation, hotkey mitigation, cache compaction markers). This has increased coupling between batching and cache lifecycles, making rollouts high-risk. Splitting responsibilities will reduce blast radius for future changes and make it easier to measure per-step latency.
acceptance_criteria: Background worker split into discrete phases (ingest, batch-finalize, cache-sync, metrics) with explicit handoff points
KV read/write surface narrowed to a single internal API with clear idempotency guarantees
End-to-end p99 generation latency reduced by >=15% on staging under identical load patterns
No increase in error rate or cache miss rate during canary (<=0.5% change)
Unit and integration tests cover handoff semantics and concurrent access patterns
technical_approach: Introduce stepper abstraction: Stage {precommit, commit, postcommit, cache-sync} with shared tracing context
Refactor existing background runner into lightweight orchestrator that invokes pure step functions
Unify KV access via kvcache.ReadWrite(ctx, key, opts) helper that enforces timeouts and backoff policies
Replace ad-hoc timer wheel in runner with centralized scheduler interface used only by the orchestrator
Add deterministic replay mode for the orchestrator to facilitate regression tests and SLO simulations
tradeoffs_and_risks: Short term: extra CPU overhead from more orchestrator scheduling hops; acceptable during canary with autoscale margin
Long term: requires retraining some on-call runbooks for new failure modes (step stuck vs whole runner stuck)
Risk of behavioral drift in kvcache semantics — mitigated by compatibility shim for 2 release cycles
testing_plan: Unit tests for new kvcache.ReadWrite semantics including idempotency and cancellation
Integration test harness that replays production trace (sanitized) through new orchestrator
Chaos test that introduces transient KV timeouts and validates graceful degradation
Staging soak for 72 hours comparing p50/p95/p99 tail distributions with existing branch
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: start with 2% of traffic routed to new orchestrator in canary namespace
Observe metrics for 24h, expand to 20% if stable, then to 100% after 7d soak
Automatic rollback on defined SLO breaches (p99 latency increase >10% or error rate spike >1%)
monitoring_and_alerts: SLO check: end-to-end generation p99 under target for the runtime-2.4 baseline
